record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the classical smoothness classes F_d^k(D_d) on volume-1 domains, explicit lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) >= min{1/2, c_k d n^(-k/d)} are known. What are the sharp values or sharper estimates of the constants c_k, and which domains D_d are extremal in the sense that, for given k, d, and n, the integration error e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) is especially small?

evidence.quote: We know from [47] the following statement for the classes Fkd (Dd) = { f : Dd -> R | ||Dalpha f||infty <= 1, |alpha| <= k} for all domains Dd with volume 1: For all k \u2208 N there exists a constant ck > 0 such that for all d,n \u2208 N e(n,Fkd (Dd)) >= min{1/2, ck d n-k/d}.

Remark 7. 1) The lower bound cannot be improved since for cubes we have a similar upper bound. It would be good to know more on the constants ck and on extremal sets Dd, where e(n,Fkd (Dd )) is small for given k, d and n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $d,k\ge 1$ and a measurable domain $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of Lebesgue volume $1$, define the smoothness class
$$F_d^k(D_d)=\{f:D_d\to\mathbb{R}\mid \|\partial^\alpha f\|_\infty\le 1\text{ for all multi-indices }\alpha\text{ with }|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
For a positive integer $n$, the (deterministic) optimal $n$-point integration error is
$$e(n,F_d^k(D_d))=\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_n\in D_d}\ \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}}\ \sup_{f\in F_d^k(D_d)}\Big|\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(x_i)\Big|.$$
It is known that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that, for all $d,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and all volume-1 domains $D_d$,
$$e(n,F_d^k(D_d))\ \ge\ \min\!\left\{\tfrac{1}{2},\ c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d}\right\}.$$
Determine the sharp (or sharper) values of the constants $c_k$ in this lower bound. Moreover, identify the extremal domains $D_d$ of volume $1$ for which, given $k$, $d$, and $n$, the integration error $e(n,F_d^k(D_d))$ is as small as possible.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent survey on optimal numerical integration. No subsequent work resolving the sharp values of $c_k$ or identifying extremal volume-1 domains was found. The lower bound is known to be tight in order on cubes, but the sharp constants and extremal sets remain undetermined.
